title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck has fixed a base point ξ0 of the moduli stack M_{g,ν} over Q, a curve X_{g,ν} over C, and a point x0 on it. He has the following groups.
- π̂_{g,ν}: the geometric fundamental group of the curve.
- T̂^+_{g,ν}: the profinite Teichmüller (mapping class) group, i.e. the geometric π1 of M_{g,ν}.
- Ĝ^+_{g,ν}: the geometric π1 of the universal curve.
- N_{g,ν} = π1(M_{g,ν,Q}) and M_{g,ν} = π1(universal curve over Q): the arithmetic fundamental groups. They are extensions of Γ_{Q̄/Q} by T̂^+ and Ĝ^+ respectively (sequence (5) of the previous page).

On this page he writes diagram (9). The top row is the arithmetic extension 1 → π̂_{g,ν} → M_{g,ν} → N_{g,ν} → 1. It maps to the tautological extension 1 → π̂ → Aut_loc(π̂) → Autext_loc(π̂) → 1. Here 'loc' means automorphisms preserving the conjugacy classes of the inertia (cusp) subgroups. The left vertical arrow is the identity. The other two vertical arrows carry '?', marking injectivity as an open question. The diagram extends the topological diagram (2) and its profinite completion (3).

Consequences he draws:
- The image M' of M_{g,ν} in Aut_loc(π̂) normalises the image T̂' of the geometric part (the 'profinite Teichmüller group').
- Formula (10): M'/T' is a quotient of Γ_{Q̄/Q}.

NB 1: one can prove that for fixed g and ν large this quotient map is an isomorphism with Γ_{Q̄/Q}. He conjectures it is always an isomorphism. The marginal addition is hard to read; it is perhaps '(& immersions)', i.e. also the injectivity of the '?' arrows.

NB 2: for g = 0 he suggests the statement is perhaps true. The critical case is ν = 3, and the statement for (0,3) is equivalent to Γ_{Q̄/Q} ↪ Autext_loc(π̂_{0,3}), i.e. Galois acting faithfully on π̂1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}). He notes that N_{0,3} ≅ T̂^+_{0,3} × N^!_{0,3}, with T^+_{0,3} = S_3 and N^!_{0,3} ≅ Γ_{Q̄/Q}. This holds because M_{0,3} over Q is BS_3 with S_3 constant.

NB 3: for g = 1 the critical case is ν = 1. The page ends there.

Purpose: to set up the 'arithmetic Teichmüller' framework, in which Γ_Q acts on the profinite Teichmüller tower through outer automorphisms of surface groups. It also isolates the minimal (critical) cases, (0,3) and (1,1), as building blocks. This is a precursor of the Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: In (10) he writes T' without the hat, whereas the line above has the hat; and he calls the image of T̂^+ (a group mapping to Autext) its image in Aut_loc. Strictly, the subgroup of Aut_loc(π̂) normalised by M' should be the image of Ĝ^+_{g,ν}, which is the preimage of T̂^+ in M_{g,ν}. This is a notational slip; the intended statement (Ĝ' normal in M', with quotient a quotient of Γ_Q) is correct.
The claim 'pour g fixé, ν grand, c'est un isom' is stated without proof. It is true; it follows from later results (Belyi; Matsumoto 1996; Hoshi–Mochizuki), but the argument is not given on the page.

The '?' on the vertical arrows is left open. For T̂ → Autext_loc(π̂_{g,ν}) this is the congruence subgroup problem for mapping class groups. It is not automatic and is still not settled in full generality, so these arrows are not known isomorphisms onto their images.

ideas.what: Diagram comparing the arithmetic extension 1→π̂→π1(universal curve/Q)→π1(M_{g,ν}/Q)→1 with the tautological extension 1→π̂→Aut_loc→Out_loc→1. It yields an outer Galois/Teichmüller representation N_{g,ν} → Out_loc(π̂_{g,ν}).
ideas.modern_name: Universal monodromy / arithmetic outer representation of the moduli stack on the profinite surface group
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §2 (Teichmüller tower, action of Γ_Q)

ideas.what: Injectivity question for T̂^+_{g,ν} → Out_loc(π̂_{g,ν}) (the '?' arrows).
ideas.modern_name: Congruence subgroup problem for mapping class groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Asada (g ≤ 1), Boggi (g = 2 and claims in general), Hoshi–Mochizuki; posed by Ivanov and others
ideas.where_published: Not explicitly formulated in Esquisse as far as I know

ideas.what: Conjecture that M'/T' ≅ Γ_{Q̄/Q} for all (g,ν), i.e. Galois acts faithfully modulo the geometric (Teichmüller) part. He claims a proof for ν large.
ideas.modern_name: Faithfulness of the Galois action on the profinite Teichmüller tower / anabelian injectivity Γ_Q ↪ Out(π̂1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Belyi 1979 (g=0), Matsumoto 1996 (affine curves), Hoshi–Mochizuki 2011 (all hyperbolic curves)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (in the form Γ_Q ↪ Out(π̂_{0,3}) via Belyi, and faithfulness on the Teichmüller tower)

ideas.what: Reduction to critical cases (0,3) and (1,1); N_{0,3} ≅ S_3 × Γ_Q, since M_{0,3} = BS_3 over Q.
ideas.modern_name: Base levels of the Teichmüller tower ('two-level principle')

missed.claim: The '?' injectivity arrows in (3) and (9) implicitly pose, in 1982, the congruence subgroup problem for mapping class groups: is T̂_{g,ν} → Out(π̂_{g,ν}) injective? He places it side by side with Galois faithfulness as a single question about the arithmetic universal curve.
missed.quote: ?∫ ... Autext_loc(π̂_{g,ν}) ... Mais je pense que c'est tjrs un iso. (& immersions?)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historically relevant to attributing the congruence subgroup problem in the anabelian setting. It is usually traced to Ivanov, Asada and Boggi rather than to Grothendieck's 1981–82 notes. The reading of the marginal note is uncertain, so the claim is modest.

missed.claim: In 1982 Grothendieck is only tentative ('peut-être') about faithfulness of Γ_Q on π̂1(P^1−{0,1,∞}), which Belyi's 1979 theorem implies. This dates his notes relative to his knowledge of Belyi's result.
missed.quote: C'est le cas peut-être pour g=0 (où le cas critique est ν=3) – ce qui équivaut à ceci que Γ_{Q̄/Q} ↪ Autext_loc(π̂_{0,3})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This bears on the chronology of the Esquisse and of Grothendieck's account of Belyi's theorem; it is historiographical rather than mathematical.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean early (1982) formulation of the Teichmüller/Galois faithfulness programme that later appears in the Esquisse. The main ideas are known and credited to him. Mildly notable are the explicit 'all (g,ν)' faithfulness conjecture with claimed proof for ν large, the implicit congruence-subgroup question, and the dating relative to Belyi.
transcription_corrections: In (9) the middle group of the bottom row is Aut_loc(π̂_{g,ν}), not Autext_loc; only the right-hand group is Autext_loc.
The left vertical arrow in (9) is an equality/isomorphism (‖ with arrow); the middle and right arrows are hook arrows marked '?' (questioned injections).
'normalise celle T̂'_{g,ν} de T̂^+_{g,ν} (le groupe "Teichmüller pro-fini") et l'image' — the parenthetical reads 'le groupe "Teichmüller pro-fini"'.
In (10) the denominator is written T'_{g,ν} (hat apparently omitted).
The marginal insertion after 'tjrs un iso.' is hard to read; possibly '(& immersions)' or '(& injections)'.
N^!_{0,3} ≅ Γ_{Q̄/Q} (written beneath, with a struck-out word before Γ).
